name: Clap the Word
mechanic: A picture word appears and its name is spoken. The child taps a big friendly drum once per syllable (kan-ga-roo = 3 taps), then releases. The drum lights and bounces on each tap; the friend nods if the tap-count matches the syllable count.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is the existing E8/E9 syllable-builder, but that is tap-to-PLACE syllable tiles spatially. Here there are no tiles and no spelling — the child PRODUCES a beat count by tapping in time, and correctness is purely the rhythmic count, not assembling letters. The output is a temporal action (N taps), not a spatial arrangement.
fun_no_competition: The drum thumps and glows under your fingers like a real instrument; the friend bobs its head to your beat, so clapping out a long word feels like drumming a little song.
character_world: A small bear band-leader with a hand drum cheering you on
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — WebAudio drum sample per tap, browser TTS for the word, tap counting in DOM; syllable counts come from the existing approved-words/vocabulary-phonics syllable data
asset_idea: stub: gray circle drum + counter. CA5: bear band-leader idle/nod/cheer, glowing drum skin with ripple frames, picture cards

name: Echo the Beat
mechanic: A character taps out a short rhythm pattern on colored pads (e.g. red-red-blue). The pads light and sound in sequence. The child then taps the SAME pads back in the same order to echo it. Pattern length grows by one as the child succeeds; the child sets the pace tapping back.
why_distinct: Not match-pairs (no pairing) and not magic-machine (no transform). The core is a call-and-RESPONSE memory-of-order: reproduce an ordered auditory/visual sequence. Closest neighbor is sticker-album sequencing, but that is free placement; here the model is given and must be echoed back in exact order, and the content is sound+order not pictures.
fun_no_competition: It feels like a musical game of follow-the-leader with a friend — each round adds one more note so you get to play a longer and longer little tune, and the pads sing back to you.
character_world: A friendly frog on a lily pad with glowing musical lily-pad buttons
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — WebAudio tones per pad, sequence playback with delays (no timer, child-paced response), DOM pad highlights
asset_idea: stub: 3 colored squares that flash. CA5: frog conductor, 4 glowing lily-pad pads with press/ripple states, twinkle sparkle on correct echo

name: Count the Beats
mechanic: A number card shows (e.g. 5). The child taps a bell that many times to 'ring out' the number; each tap adds a star to a row and plays an ascending note. When the rung count equals the number, a little fanfare plays. No counting tiles — the number is expressed as a produced sequence of beats.
why_distinct: Distinct from pop-the-right-ones (that's selecting correct targets among foils) and from any grid-fill — here the child OUTPUTS a quantity as a self-paced beat sequence, hearing the count rise. Cardinality is performed temporally (one tap = one count) rather than selected or placed.
fun_no_competition: Each ring climbs a musical scale, so counting to 5 plays do-re-mi-fa-so — you're playing a tune AND counting, and the stars line up with a sparkle when you hit the number.
character_world: A cheerful chime-mouse with a row of hanging bells
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — WebAudio ascending tones, DOM star row, tap count matched to target number
asset_idea: stub: bell button + star row. CA5: chime-mouse, swinging bell with ring frames, filling star row, confetti on match

name: Skip-Count Drum Train
mechanic: A train chugs and the child taps a drum on the BEAT to make it move, but only every Nth tap counts as a 'station stop' that speaks a skip-count number (tap-tap-TWO, tap-tap-FOUR for 2s). The child taps in groups; each completed group lands the train at the next numbered station.
why_distinct: Different from path-journey (that's choosing a route); here the path advances via a rhythmic GROUPING of taps. The math lives in the beat structure — grouping taps into twos/fives/tens and hearing the skip-count emerge — not in moving along a chosen path. Distinct from rhythm-sound-03 because it's grouped/structured counting, not flat 1-by-1.
fun_no_competition: The chugga-chugga-CHOO rhythm makes skip-counting feel like driving a train; each station arrives with a whistle and the big number, so 2-4-6-8 is a song the train sings.
character_world: A round-faced steam train with numbered stations along a track
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — WebAudio chug + whistle, TTS for the station number, tap grouping logic in DOM
asset_idea: stub: train icon + station dots. CA5: smiling train, puffing-steam frames, numbered station signs, whistle steam-burst

name: Blend it with Taps
mechanic: Three sound buttons each hold one phoneme (/c/ /a/ /t/). The child taps them left-to-right one at a time, hearing each sound; then taps a big 'blend' arrow that sweeps the buttons together faster and faster (child-controlled) until the whole word says itself. Then they tap the matching picture.
why_distinct: Not the CVC builder (no letter tiles, no spelling). The core is auditory phoneme blending PACED by the child's taps — sounds in order, then a sweep that fuses them. The skill is hearing separate sounds become a word through a temporal sweep, which no existing template does (build-a-buddy assembles parts; this fuses sounds).
fun_no_competition: Tapping the sweep arrow makes the three sounds slide together and 'magically' become a word — the satisfying moment /c/.../a/.../t/ snaps into 'cat' feels like a tiny spell working.
character_world: A gentle sound-wizard owl with three glowing sound-stones
web_shell_feasibility: needs-richer-runtime — isolated-phoneme TTS is unreliable (consonants spoken as letter names per the project's RF.K.2.c finding); requires pre-recorded phoneme audio clips per locale rather than browser TTS
asset_idea: stub: 3 sound dots + arrow. CA5: wizard owl, 3 glowing rune-stones with pulse, sweep-trail effect, picture target cards (needs phoneme audio pack)

name: Which Sound Was That?
mechanic: A sound plays (animal call, instrument, or environmental sound) and three picture choices appear. The child listens, then taps the picture that made the sound. Replayable as often as wanted by tapping the ear button. Pure listen-then-identify, fully child-paced.
why_distinct: Closest is i-spy-scene/pop-the-right-ones, but those are VISUAL search. Here the stimulus is AUDITORY and the visual is the answer set — the child decodes a sound, not scans a picture. The discrimination skill is auditory, the input modality reversed from every existing template.
fun_no_competition: It's a guessing game with your ears — the moment a 'moo' resolves into the cow is a happy little 'aha', and you can replay the sound as many times as you like, no rush.
character_world: A big-eared listening fox holding a cupped ear
web_shell_feasibility: needs-richer-runtime — requires a curated library of clean sound-effect clips (animal/instrument); WebAudio can play them but the assets must be sourced/licensed
asset_idea: stub: ear button + 3 pictures. CA5: listening fox with ear-cup animation, sound-wave ripple, picture choice cards (needs SFX audio pack)

name: Conduct the Pattern
mechanic: An AB/ABB/ABC rhythm pattern is shown as a row of colored sound-shapes that play in a loop (boom-tick-boom-tick). The next two slots are blank. The child taps from a palette of sound-shapes to FILL the blanks so the rhythm pattern continues correctly; the loop replays with their additions.
why_distinct: The platform has visual pattern-train (silent visual sequence). This makes the pattern AUDITORY+temporal — the child extends a repeating rhythm they hear looping, judging by ear/beat what comes next. The 'continue the pattern' core is real but the medium (a looping rhythm) and the judging sense (auditory) are new.
fun_no_competition: You're conducting a tiny beat-loop and the moment your added sounds keep the groove going feels like dropping the right note into a song; the loop grooves on with your additions.
character_world: A penguin conductor with a baton in front of a sound-shape music staff
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — WebAudio distinct tones per shape, looping playback, DOM pattern row with fillable slots
asset_idea: stub: colored shape row + palette. CA5: penguin conductor with baton swing, glowing sound-shapes (boom/tick/ding), looping pulse highlight

name: Rhyme Bell Match
mechanic: A word is spoken and shown as a picture. Three bells hang below, each speaking a word when tapped. The child taps bells to hear them, then taps the bell whose word RHYMES with the target. Bells chime; the matching rhyme rings a harmonious chord with the target.
why_distinct: Distinct from match-pairs (visual pairing) — the matching criterion is auditory RHYME, judged by listening to spoken words, and the 'correct' feedback is a musical harmony (rhyming words ring in tune). The child compares ending sounds by ear, a phonological-awareness skill no template targets.
fun_no_competition: When you find the rhyme, the two bells ring a sweet chord together — cat and hat literally sound good together — so finding a rhyme is rewarded with harmony, not a score.
character_world: A musical rabbit under a row of hanging hand-bells
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — browser TTS for spoken words, WebAudio chime tones layered for the harmony reward, DOM bells
asset_idea: stub: 3 bell buttons + target picture. CA5: bell-rabbit, swinging bells with ring frames, harmony sparkle when two ring together

name: Play the Number Song
mechanic: A short ascending melody of N notes plays (a 'number song'). The child watches/listens, then plays it back by tapping a row of stair-step keys in order — each key is a higher note. Reproducing the rising sequence builds a little staircase the friend climbs to the top number.
why_distinct: Different from echo-the-beat (07/02 use same-color pads / patterns) — here the keys are ORDERED by pitch+magnitude (a number line as a musical staircase), and the child plays an ascending run, connecting one-more/ordinality to rising pitch. Reproduce-an-ordered-pitch-run is its own mechanic; ties number order to sound height.
fun_no_competition: Tapping the rising keys plays a do-re-mi climb while a little character hops up the staircase — counting up literally sounds like going up, and reaching the top note is a happy bloop.
character_world: A bouncy chick hopping up a musical staircase of glowing keys
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — WebAudio ascending scale tones, DOM stair keys with press states, sequence playback (child-paced)
asset_idea: stub: row of stair keys + chick. CA5: chick hop frames, glowing staircase keys each a different height, top-of-stairs star burst

name: Sort by Syllables
mechanic: Picture-word cards drop in one at a time and are spoken. The child claps out the syllables on a tap-pad (hearing each clap), then drags the card into the bin labeled 1, 2, or 3 (claps) that matches. The clap count is the child's own measurement that decides the bin.
why_distinct: Sort-home exists, but there the sorting key is a visible category. Here the sorting key is PRODUCED by the child's own rhythmic clapping (count your claps, then sort by that count) — the act of clapping is the measurement step that no sort template includes. Distinct from clap-the-word (01) which only outputs a count; this uses the count to classify.
fun_no_competition: You become the judge — clap out the word, count your own claps, then drop the card into its bin with a satisfying plonk; the bins cheer when a card lands home.
character_world: A tidy raccoon with three labeled syllable-bins (1, 2, 3 dots)
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — clap = tap-pad with WebAudio clap sound, TTS for words, drag-to-bin DOM, syllable count from phonics data validates
asset_idea: stub: tap-pad + 3 bins + cards. CA5: raccoon, clap-pad with hand frames, three labeled bins with happy-mouth open/close, card drop dust

name: Add with Drumrolls
mechanic: Two number cards show (3 + 2). The child taps a drum 3 times (first group, low drum), then taps a second drum 2 times (second group, high drum), and the taps accumulate into one counting line; the total is heard counting up across both groups (one-two-three... four-five) and the friend announces the sum.
why_distinct: Not magic-machine (no transform box) and not match-pairs. Addition is performed as TWO rhythmic groups of taps that join into one continuous count — the 'putting together' is literally heard as one drum-roll flowing into the next. Counting-on / joining as a temporal sequence is the distinct mechanic.
fun_no_competition: Two little drum-rolls flow into one big count and the total pops out with a cymbal — joining 3 and 2 sounds like one song made of two phrases, and you played both.
character_world: A two-drum panda drummer (one low, one high)
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — WebAudio two drum samples + ascending count tones, TTS for the sum, DOM tap accumulation
asset_idea: stub: 2 drums + count row. CA5: panda drummer, two drums (low/high) with hit frames, accumulating count dots, cymbal-crash sparkle

name: Where's the Sound?
mechanic: A target sound (the first sound of a word, given as a clean syllable cue like 'sss') plays. Three picture-words are shown. The child taps each picture to HEAR it spoken, listens for which one BEGINS with that sound, and taps it. The beginning-sound is judged purely by ear.
why_distinct: The platform's beginning-sound activity is visual/letter-anchored. This version is listen-first: the child hears words and isolates onsets by ear with no letters shown — auditory onset detection. Distinct from which-sound (06, environmental sounds) because the stimulus is a SPEECH onset cue and the child probes words by listening.
fun_no_competition: Tapping each picture lets you 'try it out loud', and catching the word that starts the same way feels like an ear-detective solving a little mystery — replay all you want, no clock.
web_shell_feasibility: needs-richer-runtime — reliable onset cue ('sss', 'mmm') is fine via TTS for continuants but stops (/b/,/t/) are unreliable; best with curated onset audio for stop consonants
asset_idea: stub: ear cue + 3 pictures. CA5: detective hedgehog with monocle, sound-wave cue puff, picture cards with tap-glow

name: Hum the Pattern Up & Down
mechanic: A growing/shrinking sound pattern plays where pitch tracks a quantity (low note = small, high note = big). The child hears a sequence (small-big-small) and arranges three picture-objects of different sizes in the order the sounds went, using pitch as the size cue.
why_distinct: Maps an auditory dimension (pitch) onto a math attribute (size/quantity) and asks the child to ORDER objects by decoding the sound sequence. Distinct from big-small/sort templates which are silent-visual; here the ordering information arrives as sound and must be translated. Cross-modal pitch-to-size ordering is novel.
fun_no_competition: Low notes feel small and high notes feel big — when you line up the objects to match the tune you 'see the sound', and the row plays back its little melody to confirm.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — WebAudio pitch sweep tones, DOM drag-order of 3 size-graded picture objects, playback confirmation
asset_idea: stub: 3 pitch dots + 3 objects. CA5: singing whale, rising/falling bubble-notes, size-graded object cards (small/med/big), order-confirm shimmer

name: Stretch the Word
mechanic: A picture-word is shown. The child presses and HOLDS a stretch-button: as they hold, the spoken word slows and pulls apart into its sounds (rubber-band style), and dots appear for each phoneme heard. Releasing snaps it back to the whole word. The child then taps the dot-count that matches.
why_distinct: A press-and-hold 'stretchy speech' interaction — phoneme segmentation made tangible by slowing the word and counting the sounds that pop out. No template uses hold-to-stretch audio. Distinct from blend (05) which fuses sounds; this SEGMENTS them, and the gesture (hold/stretch) is the core.
fun_no_competition: Holding the button stretches 'fish' into f-i-sh like pulling taffy, and the sound-dots pop out one by one — it's playful and physical, and letting go snaps the word back together with a boing.
character_world: A stretchy rubber-band cat that pulls words apart
web_shell_feasibility: needs-richer-runtime — smooth time-stretch of speech needs pre-segmented per-phoneme audio (or a playbackRate trick on recorded clips); browser TTS can't cleanly stretch into phonemes
asset_idea: stub: hold-button + dot row. CA5: rubber-band cat stretch frames, taffy-pull word visual, phoneme dots popping, snap-back boing effect

name: Tap the Tens & Ones Beat
mechanic: A two-digit number shows (e.g. 23). The child taps a deep 'TEN' gong for each ten (low boom × 2) then a light 'ONE' tick for each one (× 3). The two grouped rhythms — booms then ticks — sonify the place value, and the friend says 'two tens and three ones, twenty-three' when the beat matches.
why_distinct: Place value performed as a TWO-LAYER rhythm (heavy beats for tens, light beats for ones). Distinct from the platform's visual place-value build-on-columns engine — here the decomposition is heard and tapped, not stacked as blocks. Sonifying tens-vs-ones as distinct beat weights is a new mechanic.
fun_no_competition: Big booms for tens and tiny ticks for ones make a number into a little rhythm pattern — 23 has its own beat, and tapping it out makes place value feel like drumming.
character_world: A two-gong tortoise: a big gong (tens) and a tiny bell (ones)
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — WebAudio low gong + high tick samples, TTS for the decomposition, DOM tap grouping with place-value check
asset_idea: stub: big gong + small bell + count. CA5: tortoise drummer, large gong with deep-ripple, small bell with light-ring, tens/ones beat dots

name: Read it to the Beat
mechanic: A short decodable sentence is shown with one tap-pad per word. The child taps each pad in order at their own pace; each tap speaks that word and the character takes one step. Tapping word-by-word in sequence reads the sentence aloud and walks the character to the end — a paced, left-to-right read.
why_distinct: Different from story-maker (assembling a story) — this is concept-of-print: one tap = one word, in order, left to right, with one-to-one speech-to-word correspondence. The temporal one-tap-per-word pacing instantiates tracking print, which no template targets. The rhythm IS reading word-by-word.
fun_no_competition: Each tap makes the character take a step and says the word, so reading the sentence walks your friend across the page to a little goal — finishing the line feels like completing a short journey you read aloud.
character_world: A snail crossing a leaf, one word-step at a time
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — browser TTS per word, DOM word-pads in order, character step animation; decodable sentences from existing word data
asset_idea: stub: word pads + walker dot. CA5: stepping snail frames, word-pads that light when tapped, finish-leaf with sparkle

name: Equal Beats
mechanic: Two short rhythm rows play (e.g. left = 3 claps, right = 5 claps). The child listens to both, then taps the side with MORE beats (or a 'same' button when equal). Each row replays on tap; comparison is made by ear, counting beats, not by seeing a quantity.
why_distinct: Compare-quantity exists as silent visual (more-less/big-small). Here the two quantities are presented as RHYTHMIC beat-sequences and compared by listening and counting beats — auditory magnitude comparison. The stimulus modality and the count-by-listening are new versus every visual comparison template.
fun_no_competition: Listening to two little beat-bursts and feeling which one is longer is like comparing two drum solos — replay them as much as you want and the friend nods when you pick the bigger beat.
character_world: Two friendly drum-bugs side by side, each with its own beat
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — WebAudio clap sequences per side, replay on tap, DOM more/same/less choice
asset_idea: stub: two drum buttons + choice. CA5: two drum-bugs, beat-burst ripple per side, 'more/same' big buttons, winner-side gentle glow
